scope_note: US-market Dodge Ramcharger 1974-1993 (AW100/AW150 4WD from mid-1974; AD100/AD150 2WD from 1975). Plymouth Trail Duster (PW/PD, 1974-1981) is the same truck; its brochures are used as Chrysler literature and its trims noted. The Mexico-only Ramcharger (Mexican production of the old body continued to 1996; a Ram-based 2WD version with 5.2/5.9 Magnum V8s was sold 1999-2001) is out of scope.

Independent source groups: Chrysler/Dodge/Plymouth literature (all brochures = 1), Flory (1; Google Books snippets - powertrain tables have a Ramcharger availability column that snippets do not render, so Flory rows show the engine existed that year, not always that the Ramcharger had it), Wikipedia (1), EPA (1984+, size/cylinders only), Consumer Guide (1), Curbside Classic (1), Hagerty Media (1), Hagerty valuation text (1, weak), Drivingline, Sports Car Market, Automobile Magazine. Wikipedia/Hagerty/Curbside/Automobile/Drivingline gen-1 statements are generation-level engine lists, not year-specific; they are counted as supporting only where a year-specific source places the engine in that year. No Ramcharger brochure online for 1974, 1975, 1980, 1981, 1982, 1984-1986, 1989, 1992. NHRA has no Ramcharger rows. No Chrysler 3.9 V6, 225 six after 1981, diesel, or 318 4-bbl after 1983 was found for the Ramcharger. Wikipedia/Hagerty/Curbside state the 225 was standard from launch; Sports Car Market, Flory and the Consumer Guide 1974 ad review show 1974 was V8-only with the 318 standard.
